facts.statement: The genus Mcmurdodus was described by White in 1968.
The species Mcmurdodus featherensis lived in Antarctica during the Middle Devonian period.
facts.quote: from the Middle Devonian of Antarctica

facts.statement: Mcmurdodus is classified as an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish within the family Mcmurdodontidae.
facts.quote: Mcmurdodus is an extinct genus of chondrichthyan belonging to the family Mcmurdodontidae

facts.statement: Recent analyses suggest that the family Mcmurdodontidae is now considered indeterminate among chondrichthyans.
facts.quote: the Mcmurdontidae are now considered indeterminate chondrichthyans

facts.statement: It is debated whether Mcmurdodus belongs to the Hexanchiformes because it lacks multiple layers of enameloid on its tooth crowns, a feature found in all modern sharks.
facts.quote: more recent analyses indicate that they lack multiple layers of enameloid on their tooth crowns, something present in all modern sharks

facts.statement: There is a scientific disagreement regarding Mcmurdodus's classification because most divergence estimates for modern sharks do not align with the age of this genus.
facts.quote: most divergence estimates for modern sharks are irreconcilable with the age of Mcmurdodus

facts.statement: The Australian species M. whitei was originally placed in Mcmurdodus but was reclassified into the new genus Maiseyodus in 2021.
facts.quote: The Australian species M. whitei was previously included in the genus too, but was moved to a new genus, Maiseyodus, in 2021

rejected.statement: The teeth of Mcmurdodus closely resemble those of modern sharks in the families Hexanchidae and Echinorhinidae.
rejected.quote: Their teeth closely resemble those of modern sharks in the families Hexanchidae and Echinorhinidae
